key_insight: The paper proves the Fong-Tsui conjecture in full generality: for bounded operators on any complex Hilbert space, the condition |T| \u2264 |Re T| forces T to be self-adjoint.
engineering_relevance: It gives a dimension-independent operator-theoretic criterion and a quantitative stability bound that can guide robust analysis in functional analysis, operator inequalities, and related verification workflows.
method: Use a positive inverse of a Sylvester map to set up the core vanishing argument.
Apply a spectral cutoff based on the norm of the defect |Re T| - |T|.
Reduce locally to a squared self-adjointness criterion, then obtain a global contradiction from positivity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a proof over arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces plus a quantitative estimate, but it does not describe experimental data; validation is theoretical and proof-based.
watch_item: The stability exponent is stated as non-optimal, so the quantitative bound should be treated as a provable guarantee rather than a sharp estimate.
paper_title: A General Proof of the Fong-Tsui Conjecture
